last_update.summary: Bookmark phishing attacks targeting the FOMO web platform are emerging, according to monitoring by SlowMist's Cos reported by PANews on October 8. The phishing pages trick users into completing a fake human verification step, which drags a malicious JavaScript snippet into the browser's bookmarks and saves it there as a bookmark. Once a user clicks on the bookmark two to three times, their previously logged-in FOMO account is hijacked by attackers, who then immediately steal the crypto assets held inside. The report describes the attack mechanism as observed through SlowMist's monitoring; it does not state a specific event time, the number of affected users, or the value of assets stolen.

prior_items.title: Fomo acquires Mobula for $17M as weekly trading volume tops $1B
prior_items.summary:
Social trading app Fomo has acquired the proprietary software and intellectual property of onchain data company Mobula in a $17 million deal, with key members of Mobula's team joining Fomo's engineering organization. SolanaFloor reports that Mobula founder Sacha Marcus, CTO Sacha Delhoux, and Head of Infrastructure Cyril Conan are joining Fomo. Mobula's technology already powered parts of Fomo's infrastructure, including real-time APIs and security-enriched data endpoints used for scam detection and social discovery. Mobula is reportedly continuing to operate independently while Fomo takes control of its core intellectual property and engineering leadership. According to the press release, the deal is meant to help Fomo build more of its onchain data and global infrastructure capabilities internally rather than depend on multiple external providers, with the company citing growing demands on its infrastructure as it adds users, markets, and new trading products. CEO Paul Erlanger said, 'As fomo scales, we're investing in technology that will support the next phase of the business.'

The deal comes during a period of rapid growth that the outlet describes as putting a strain on Fomo's technical infrastructure; on August 30, the platform notified users of an outage that disrupted cross-chain trading. Fomo now has more than 1.9 million users, more than double its total from the beginning of July, and is adding more than 30,000 users per day. More than 1.2 million users traded or interacted with the platform in August, and the app climbed as high as No. 3 in the U.S. Finance category on Apple's iPhone App Store, surpassing Cash App. Dune data showed Fomo reaching a record 107,000 daily traders on August 25. Trading volume has accelerated alongside user growth: monthly volume rose from $500 million in June to $1.5 billion in July, and last week the platform recorded an all-time high of $1.06 billion in weekly trading volume, including $356.56 million from Solana.

The article attributes the expansion to Fomo's combination of trading, asset discovery, and social interaction, in which users follow traders, discover tokens through others' activity, and build audiences around performance. The product has broadened beyond its original offering: Fomo Web now generates roughly 25% of platform volume, Fomo Perpetuals continues to grow, and the Clans feature lets trader communities organize and compete together. The article also notes Fomo's rise has intensified its competition with Pump.fun, particularly around SocialFi and memecoin trading. Per the article, the acquisition gives Fomo more control over a layer of its business that grows more central as trading activity increases, since reliable onchain data underpins execution quality for users.

prior_items.title: BitGo CEO Mike Belshe says digital assets are going mainstream, with or without Congress
prior_items.summary:
On October 7, 2026, BitGo co-founder and CEO Mike Belshe told Bloomberg at Token2049 in Singapore that digital assets are joining the mainstream financial system 'whether the US Congress acts or not,' framing adoption as advancing regardless of what US lawmakers do. Token2049 Singapore runs October 7 to 8, and Belshe is scheduled to appear on the Institutional Stage on October 8 for a session on what regulatory clarity means for institutional strategy in crypto.

Around the interview, the article points to BitGo's Asia-Pacific expansion. The company's Singapore trading desk is now its largest anywhere in the world, according to the report. BitGo, which trades publicly under the ticker BTGO, ties that growth to the Major Payment Institution licence it obtained in 2024, reporting that its APAC client base has tripled since the licence was granted, regional headcount has more than doubled, and regional trading volumes more than doubled in the first half of 2026.

The article also notes that on October 6, during the Token2049 window, BitGo and HashKey Cloud formalized a strategic partnership spanning staking, trading, custody, and real-world asset tokenization, which the report describes as deepening BitGo's regional ties.

Separately, the report notes Belshe has positioned prime brokerage as BitGo's target revenue driver, with a stated aim for prime brokerage to become 100% of revenue rather than relying on standalone custody fees, and says the HashKey deal's service mix fits into that vision as the article frames it.

For readers following BTGO, the article closes by framing the company's story as increasingly about Asia and revenue mix, holding up Singapore's licensing framework as a practical example of how a defined regulatory regime can attract institutional business. The piece was edited by John Chen, per its disclosure.

prior_items.title: BitGo Bank & Trust brings Lido ETH staking to eligible US clients
prior_items.summary: On October 7, 2026, BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. announced that eligible US clients can stake Ether through Lido directly inside their existing BitGo accounts, with staking, the stETH receipt and ongoing position management handled in one place, according to a Crypto Briefing report. Clients stake ETH and receive stETH, Lido's liquid staking token, which represents a staked position and remains transferable while the underlying ETH stays staked; the approach avoids traditional lock-up periods, per the article's explainer. The report says BitGo's US clients will not need to set up extra operational workflows or bring in additional counterparties, and it describes BitGo as positioned to be the first US-based qualified custodian to offer native ETH staking through Lido, a first-mover characterization attributed to the companies. Kean Gilbert, Head of Institutional Relations at the Lido Ecosystem Foundation, framed the move as supplying the custodial backing institutions need to pursue Lido staking strategies. Nathan Stump, Managing Director at BitGo, emphasized keeping BitGo's controls in place while letting the service plug into clients' existing asset management infrastructure. Figures cited in the report put BitGo's custody platform at more than $100 billion in digital assets, of which $48 billion is designated as staked, and Lido at more than $25 billion in staked ETH — over 25% of all staked ETH and the leading liquid staking protocol by market share. Per the article, the US launch builds on a July 2025 rollout that connected BitGo clients in Europe and Asia to Lido's staking services, giving the two companies more than a year of operating history before extending the offer to US clients. It describes the most direct impact as falling on US institutions already custodying ETH with BitGo, which can pursue staking yield through Lido without changing custodians or rebuilding their operational stack, and suggests the regulated US distribution channel could reinforce Lido's lead while giving rival custodians a benchmark to neutralize. Separately from this announcement, BitGo had other institutional news in the same week per prior reports — an October 6 partnership signing between BitGo and HashKey Cloud covering staking, trading, custody and tokenization, and an October 5 Grayscale 8-K naming BitGo Bank & Trust an additional custodian for its Hyperliquid Staking ETF — but the report does not connect either to this launch. The companies did not disclose staking fees, detailed eligibility criteria or an availability timeline in the report.

prior_items.title: BitGo and HashKey expand institutional partnership
prior_items.summary: On October 6, 2026, at 08:00 UTC, BitGo Holdings and HashKey Cloud announced a strategic partnership covering staking, trading, custody and real-world asset tokenization for eligible institutional clients in Asia-Pacific. The companies signed the agreement at the Fullerton Bay Hotel in Singapore during TOKEN2049 week. BitGo signed with WanCloud Ltd., the HashKey Group company that operates as HashKey Cloud. Abel Seow, BitGo's managing director and head of APAC sales, and Leo Li, CEO of HashKey OnChain BG, represented the companies at the ceremony. Per the announcement, the signing extends a staking collaboration the two companies began in July into a broader relationship. The agreement is divided into four service lines. HashKey Cloud will become a validator partner on BitGo's platform, with initial staking support covering Ethereum and Solana for eligible BitGo institutional clients; the release describes those two networks as the starting set without naming additional assets or a date for adding them. On custody, BitGo will make its custody services available to HashKey Capital and associated funds, subject to customary onboarding and separate agreements — the announcement establishes a framework and does not show that any fund's assets have moved into BitGo custody. For tokenized real-world assets, BitGo will become a custody partner for HashKey's initiatives, though the release names no asset, issuer, chain or planned issuance and does not specify whether BitGo would hold the underlying asset, the on-chain token, reserve assets or a combination. The trading component is the least defined: the companies said HashKey Cloud and BitGo will collaborate to support institutional trading flow, without identifying venues, settlement arrangements, order types, asset coverage or which entity would face each client. No transaction value or launch schedule was disclosed for any part of the agreement. The release limits every described service to eligible clients and jurisdictions where the activity is permitted, and provides no staking fee terms, validator performance standards, slashing allocation or withdrawal mechanics. HashKey Cloud describes itself as HashKey Holding's institutional staking and Web3 infrastructure arm, providing node validation services since 2018; BitGo says it operates multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association. The companies describe the combined offer as serving institutions across the asset lifecycle, while each workstream remains separately defined — the announcement does not say that HashKey Capital will use HashKey Cloud as validator, that trading clients must use BitGo custody, or that a tokenized asset must use the new staking connection.

prior_items.title: BitGo and HashKey Cloud expand staking partnership into trading, custody and RWA tokenization
prior_items.summary:
BitGo and HashKey Cloud have expanded their existing staking partnership into institutional trading, custody and real-world asset tokenization, according to a crypto.news report. BitGo said on Oct. 6 that the companies signed the expanded agreement in Singapore during TOKEN2049 week, with WanCloud Ltd. — which operates as HashKey Cloud within HashKey Group — signing with NYSE-listed BitGo Holdings. The agreement covers four business areas — staking, institutional trading flow, custody and real-world asset (RWA) tokenization — and services are limited to eligible institutional customers and jurisdictions where the relevant products are permitted. The report says the companies disclosed no financial terms, launch schedule, initial customers or expected assets under management.

Staking is the continuation of work the two companies had already begun. Their first partnership, announced in July, centered on institutional staking and was designed to let institutional clients participate in proof-of-stake networks while keeping their assets within BitGo's custody framework, with HashKey Cloud supplying the validator infrastructure. The new agreement makes HashKey Cloud a validator partner on BitGo's platform, with Ethereum and Solana as the first supported staking assets for eligible institutional clients. The article notes that neither company has given an exact date for expanded staking access or identified the first clients expected to use the service, and that the Oct. 6 announcement did not disclose fees, staking reward terms or how much ETH and SOL could enter the arrangement. HashKey Cloud has operated blockchain validation infrastructure since 2018, and its website lists staking products for institutions, asset managers and professional investors across multiple blockchain networks.

On trading, the companies said they will work together to support institutional trading flow, though the announcement did not identify exchanges, trading pairs or expected volumes. Per the report, BitGo already runs trading and settlement infrastructure alongside its custody business, its Singapore entity holds a Major Payment Institution license covering digital payment token services and cross-border money transfers according to the Monetary Authority of Singapore's financial institutions register, and BitGo recently expanded an off-exchange settlement arrangement with OKX under which supported assets can remain in segregated custody at BitGo Singapore while eligible institutions outside the U.S. access exchange liquidity. The article states that the HashKey agreement does not say that same setup will automatically apply to the new trading relationship.

Custody terms are more specific: BitGo will make its custody services available to HashKey Capital and associated funds, subject to client onboarding and separate agreements. The report cites BitGo platform figures for the end of June — 5,833 clients, $65.2 billion in assets on the platform, $11.9 billion in assets staked and second-quarter staking revenue of $64.7 million.

On real-world assets, BitGo will serve as a custody partner for HashKey's tokenization initiatives across Asia-Pacific markets. The report relays HashKey's first-half 2026 figures — HK$2.68 billion in onchain RWA total value locked, up 167.8% from a year earlier, with institutional customers accounting for HK$231.5 billion of its HK$282.2 billion platform trading volume, or 82% — and says HashKey's tokenization work has included regulated products in Hong Kong, a recent move by HashKey Exchange to distribute Franklin Templeton's tokenized U.S. government money market fund to eligible professional investors, and a September arrangement with Prometheum Capital and Velocity Capital covering a proposed route for tokenized U.S. equities that remains subject to final agreements, regulatory clearance and technical work. The report presents those items as HashKey's existing activity rather than as components of the BitGo agreement.

Abel Seow, BitGo's managing director and head of APAC sales, said institutions in Asia are seeking infrastructure covering several stages of digital asset activity. Leo Li, CEO of HashKey OnChain BG, described the combination of HashKey's Hong Kong presence and BitGo's custody infrastructure as a 'trusted pathway across staking, trading, custody, and tokenization.'

prior_items.title: After Proposal 613's cancellation, a Compound forum proposal would move EPCF and SVR custody from Foundation-controlled Safes to the Community Multisig
prior_items.summary: Compound forum user ugurmersin posted a proposal outline on comp.xyz on October 8, 2026, one day after the Proposal Guardian cancelled Proposal 613 on October 7. The alternative would leave the EPCF (Ecosystem Protection and Continuity Fund) open but change who holds the keys: per the post, the EPCF's holdings — 500,000 USDC plus 4,583,411 USDC supplied to cUSDCv3 — and the mainnet Chainlink SVR revenue of 355.95 ETH would move from Safes the Compound Foundation controls alone to the Community Multisig, which acts by five-of-nine signer approval. The author says the EPCF would keep its purposes, size and 48-month term, with emergency deployment still available, distinguishing the plan from Proposal 613, which he writes would have closed the fund and sent everything to the Governor Timelock over objections including pennblockchain's that this removed the fund's rapid-response role. Arguing that DAO funds elsewhere sit behind a committee, a withdrawal cooldown and reclamation paths while these two pools do not, the author notes both Safes are controlled by the same two addresses. As context for why custody matters now, he recounts on-chain activity around the V2 reserves granted under Proposal 536 — including COMP arrivals close to governance voting snapshots, a 912,717 COMP vote for Proposal 580, transfers routed through wallets to eight exchanges, and USDT returned to the Safe — which he characterizes as misappropriation. The Foundation disputes that characterization and stated in a September 28 forum post that there has been no trading; the author concedes exchange-internal trades are not visible on-chain and asks the Foundation to publish its trading-firm agreement and transfer records. He argues the Community Multisig, nine organizations that already hold the DAO's Pause Guardian, Treasury Escrow Safeguard and Proposal Guardian roles, is a stronger check than two signers from one organization, while saying he still views its composition as imperfect and the proposal as the minimum rather than the ideal.

prior_items.title: Compound DAO considers extending treasury safeguards under heightened oversight
prior_items.summary: Compound DAO is voting on Proposal 612, submitted by Ugur Mersin, which would extend the Treasury Escrow withdrawal cooldown and Treasury Timelock minimum delay from two days to ten. The proposal would also give the Governor Timelock authority to execute or cancel Treasury Timelock actions and set a 17-day Escrow expiration, leaving a seven-day withdrawal window after the cooldown. Voting opened October 4, 2026, and was scheduled to end October 7. A wallet linked to delegate Humpy had cast 1.75 million COMP in favor, while 921,000 COMP opposed the measure, according to Crypto Briefing. The proposal follows recent Treasury Management Committee activity, including a September 29 transfer of $3 million in stablecoins and a $2 million USDC deployment into a Uniswap V3 COMP position. The article also referenced allegations that the Compound Foundation exchanged 8.42 million DAI for about 344,780 COMP before important governance votes, while noting that the claims had not been established as findings.

prior_items.title: Bitdeer sets January 2027 start for 901 capacity delivery and 67 MW target by Q2 2027
prior_items.summary:
Bitdeer Technologies Group has laid out a delivery schedule for its next data center build-out, saying it plans to begin delivering capacity for its 901 site in January 2027 and to reach 67 MW by the second quarter of that year. The Singapore-based company, which trades on Nasdaq under BTDR, has been stacking up capacity commitments for its AI Cloud and high-performance computing business, much of it in Malaysia.

The 901 schedule sits alongside the company's A201 data center in Johor Bahru, which carries roughly 21.7 MW of IT capacity. Bitdeer states that off-take commitments cover more than 70% of A201, that the facility is expected to energize in the first quarter of 2027, and that the contracted capacity is expected to generate more than $1.7 billion in revenue over five years. Next door, the A202 site adds 65.1 MW and targets energization in the third quarter of 2027 under a 10-year agreement, bringing the Johor Bahru campus to a planned 86.8 MW. The smaller A102 site, at 9.5 MW, is fully contracted and expected to contribute more than $800 million.

Following the A201 commitments, Bitdeer puts its expected AI Cloud revenue backlog at around $2.9 billion. The company maintains a target of up to 350 MW of AI Cloud capacity by the first quarter of 2028, with recent announcements bringing secured capacity to approximately 333.5 MW. Per the article, the 350 MW plan is financed largely through customer prepayments and contractual financing, meaning clients effectively help fund the facilities they will use.

Bitdeer continues to operate as a vertically integrated Bitcoin mining company with operations in several countries, and says it can allocate electricity flexibly between mining and AI services using infrastructure originally built for Bitcoin. It has also been designated a preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner, and between September and October 2026 it pushed forward on GPU procurement and signed incremental site agreements.

The article frames the January 2027 start, the Q2 2027 ramp, and the A201 and A202 energization dates as plans rather than completed milestones. It notes that a meaningful share of the contracted capacity sits on a single Malaysian campus, so local permitting, power supply, or policy changes could ripple through several projects at once, and identifies the near-term checkpoints as the 901 delivery start in January 2027, A201's Q1 2027 energization, and whether the gap between roughly 333.5 MW secured and the 350 MW goal closes before Q1 2028.

prior_items.title: HIVE Digital Technologies plans Phase 3 expansion to 400 MW at Paraguay hydro campus
prior_items.summary:
HIVE Digital Technologies is adding another 100 MW to its hydroelectric data center campus in Yguazú, Paraguay — a Phase 3 build that would bring the site's total capacity to 400 MW, all of it drawn from the Itaipú Dam. The company is targeting completion by Q3 2026, and states that if the schedule holds, the campus would become the largest hydro-powered facility in Paraguay.

The build continues a staged rollout: HIVE bought the Yguazú data center from Bitfarms in January 2025, brought Phase 1 online in April 2025 at 200 MW, and followed with Phase 2 in September 2025, lifting the site to 300 MW. At its current size, the campus produces approximately 8.5 BTC per day, per company reporting. Since the acquisition, HIVE says it has committed more than $400 million to its Paraguay operations, with $130 million of that toward construction costs and the remainder covering taxes and other buildout.

The added capacity feeds into a broader company target: HIVE aims to reach 35 exahashes per second of global Bitcoin mining capacity by the end of 2026, up from 22 EH/s as of October 2025.

Bitcoin is only part of the Paraguay plan. The company also intends to build out high-performance computing and AI infrastructure, planning a dedicated AI factory powered by a new 100 MW substation that it anticipates will come online in the second half of 2027, alongside a stated goal of scaling its HPC and AI capabilities fivefold.

HIVE, which trades on the TSX Venture Exchange and Nasdaq under the ticker HIVE, points to the Itaipú Dam's hydroelectric abundance as Paraguay's appeal, letting it lock in competitive energy rates in an industry where electricity is often the biggest operating cost. The company also participates in demand response, adjusting its power usage with grid needs. Gabriel Lamas, HIVE's Country President in Paraguay, has framed the company as a contributor to the nation's energy resilience, arguing that its ability to modulate demand helps stabilize the grid rather than simply drain it.

The article frames Phase 3 as the test of whether HIVE's 2025 execution pace holds, flags concentration risk in placing a large share of growth in a single country and a single power source, and points to the Q3 2026 completion target, changes in daily Bitcoin output once the new capacity is live, and the 2027 AI factory timeline as milestones to watch.

prior_items.title: Matter Labs open-sources Prividium permissioning engine; Deutsche Bundesbank tests self-hosted instance
prior_items.summary:
Matter Labs, the company behind the ZKsync protocol, made the core permissioning engine of its Prividium enterprise blockchain platform publicly available on September 8, 2026, releasing the code under the Apache 2.0 license. According to the publication's report, the release covers one main application and six packages in a public GitHub repository, matter-labs/prividium-core.

Germany's Deutsche Bundesbank is the first organization testing a self-hosted instance of Prividium, the report states, and is collaborating with Matter Labs on both design and testing for its deployment. The report presents this as a test rather than a production rollout.

The permissioning engine is the component that decides who can do what on a private chain — a layer the publication says carries particular weight for regulated institutions, where permissions and auditability are central compliance concerns. Its release completes a stack whose other pieces — ZKsync OS, the Atlas sequencer, the Airbender prover, and the interoperability contracts — had already been open-sourced. With the engine public, the report says institutions can now independently build permissioned chains using publicly shared code; previously, the gatekeeping layer was the missing piece of the publicly available stack.

Under the Apache 2.0 license, the report notes, institutions can inspect and modify the engine without signing a commercial agreement for that specific component — a bank can read every line, change what it needs, and run it in-house without needing Matter Labs' permission.

The release is not total. Matter Labs is keeping its enterprise tooling — user interfaces and deployment tools — proprietary, an arrangement the publication characterizes as giving away the engine while selling the car built around it.

Matter Labs framed the open-source move as a response to institutional feedback, saying large organizations had voiced wariness about depending on a single vendor for critical technology, per the report. Prividium is built for validium-style chains in which transaction data stays off-chain for privacy while the chain anchors to Ethereum through zero-knowledge proofs; the publication notes that institutional adoption of this model would route more enterprise activity back to Ethereum as the settlement layer.

The report also points to the limits of the open engine on its own: institutions that self-host still need the skills to run and maintain the stack, which the proprietary deployment tools exist to address.

prior_items.title: Hyperscale Data's Ault Markets opens live, invite-only access to beta DEX on Ault Blockchain
prior_items.summary: Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS) said in an Oct. 8, 2026 press release that Ault Markets is now providing live, invite-only access to the decentralized exchange (DEX) currently operating in beta format on the Ault Blockchain. Per the release, Ault Markets, Inc. created the Ault Markets software to provide access to the DEX, which launched natively on the Ault Blockchain, and — following the model of other decentralized exchanges — listing decisions and trading on the exchange are not controlled by a centralized entity. The company framed the launch as following its previously announced plans to develop the exchange and expand its blockchain-based financial technology offerings. Access remains by invitation only: interested participants can visit AultMarkets.com to request an invitation and join a list for updates on new assets and platform developments. Hyperscale Data said it plans to substantially expand the range of assets available on Ault Markets and tradeable on the DEX, with planned additions including tokenized silver, tokenized gold and tokenized platinum, and that further announcements will provide details as those products progress toward launch. Executive Chairman Milton 'Todd' Ault III said the company had been developing Ault Markets 'for some time' and had shared its progress 'through a series of press releases over the past year and a half,' adding, 'The platform we have been discussing is now live, and we are very proud of the work that our team and our core contributors accomplished to reach this milestone.' He also said the company believes tokenization will be one of the most important developments in financial markets over the next 10 years, with the potential to change how people access, own and trade assets, and that the company is proud to have Ault Markets positioned to participate in that opportunity. The company said it will continue to update stockholders and interested participants as the invitation-only rollout progresses and additional assets are introduced. The release did not state when the access went live, which assets are currently listed on the beta DEX, or when the planned tokenized metals could launch, and it included no figures on users or trading activity.

The company is targeting $300 million to $350 million in 2027 revenue and $60 million to $80 million in adjusted EBITDA, and it previously estimated the campus could be worth $750 million to $1.25 billion. At the event, management plans to update investors on an agreement with a California-based neocloud provider covering an initial 20 MW of AI compute capacity targeted to launch in November 2026, with options to expand to 52 MW — a deployment the company projects could generate more than $3 billion in revenue over 20 years. Hyperscale Data, which says it has already invested more than $70 million in subsidiary Alliance Cloud Services and the Michigan site, estimates the campus could ultimately support over 300 MW, depending on financing, approvals, infrastructure, and demand. Management also said it will likely discuss strategic options for two subsidiaries, Sentinum, Inc. and askROI, Inc. Separately, the company has previously announced plans to move its Bitcoin mining operations into Patriot BTC, splitting them from its Michigan and Montana data centers so the Michigan campus can focus on AI compute. The Investor Day agenda also covers Hyperscale's defense, energy, real estate, finance, and technology businesses, plus blockchain initiatives at Ault Markets, Inc. Executive Chairman Milton "Todd" Ault III said, "We are focused on delivering the contracted capacity in our Michigan Campus and turning that investment into cash flow." At the time of publication on Monday, Hyperscale Data shares were up 1.80% at $0.17, according to Benzinga Pro data.

prior_items.title: Hyperscale Data shuts down Michigan Bitcoin mining to convert the site into an AI data center
prior_items.summary:
Per a September 3 report by PANews, citing Cointelegraph, Hyperscale Data has shut down its Bitcoin mining operations at its Michigan facility in order to convert the site into an AI data center. The company said all miners at the site have been powered off and that it plans to sell the related mining equipment.

The company stated that a customer has signed a contract for 20 megawatts of AI computing capacity at the facility over a 10-year term that includes two five-year renewal options. Per the report, the contract is expected to generate more than $1.2 billion in revenue over 20 years, and an additional 32-megawatt option could push potential revenue above $3 billion. These figures are presented as company projections and are not independently verified in the report, which does not identify the customer.

The report says Hyperscale is financing the transition by selling its Bitcoin holdings: per the article, the company's holdings fell from about 1,006 BTC at the end of July to 215 BTC, a decline of about 79% that dropped it to 84th among publicly traded companies ranked by Bitcoin holdings. The article does not state at what prices the holdings were sold or how much the sales raised.

Per the report, Hyperscale Data's stock fell about 17% on Wednesday to $0.1984, which the article describes as a new all-time low on a split-adjusted basis. The article gives no specific timestamps for the shutdown, the contract signing, or the Bitcoin sales, and anchors the share-price decline only to an unnamed Wednesday.

prior_items.title: SoftBank weighs a deal for Allied Universal valued at up to $18 billion
prior_items.summary:
SoftBank Group is reportedly in early discussions to acquire Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the United States, in a potential deal that could value Allied's equity at up to $18 billion, according to reporting. The talks are described as preliminary: no decisions have been made on price or deal structure, and both SoftBank and Allied Universal declined to comment.

The market reaction was negative. SoftBank's American Depositary Receipts (ticker SFTBY) fell roughly 9.5% to 10% after the news surfaced on October 16, 2026.

The reported equity figure is only part of the cost. Allied Universal carries about $12 billion in publicly traded debt, which would put a deal's total enterprise value at potentially near $30 billion. The company is currently backed by private equity firm Warburg Pincus and Canadian pension fund manager La Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec; the reporting does not detail their stance on a potential sale, though any transaction would presumably need their buy-in.

As reported, the rationale is that SoftBank wants to integrate AI and robotics into physical infrastructure and day-to-day operations, and Allied Universal's large workforce and wide network of sites could serve as a testing ground — making SoftBank a built-in customer of its own technology rather than a vendor selling robots to security firms. Deploying humanoid robots in such settings is described as a longer-term goal. Allied also has a growing line of work supporting data centers, the facilities AI systems run on, and offers security staffing for corporate clients and events.

The article situates the move within SoftBank's broader AI-related commitments, including a $30 billion commitment to OpenAI and its earlier $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics business.

The article's assessment is that the share drop suggests shareholders are worried about the size and complexity of a potential deal, that layering a near-$30 billion enterprise value on top of the OpenAI commitment raises questions about how much capital SoftBank is tying up in long-dated bets, and that taking on about $12 billion in Allied obligations would add leverage to a company already watched for balance-sheet stretch. It also notes that security services is a low-margin, labor-intensive business requiring a different skill set than venture investing or funding AI labs.

Per the article, the key things to watch are whether the talks advance past the early stage, what price and structure emerge, and how SoftBank proposes to finance the deal.

prior_items.title: SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son reportedly in preliminary talks to raise up to $100 billion for a new AI fund
prior_items.summary:
SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son is in preliminary talks with senior officials from Gulf nations, particularly the United Arab Emirates, to raise up to $100 billion for a new artificial intelligence fund, according to an October 9, 2026 Financial Times report cited in the article. SoftBank has not officially confirmed the discussions. Bloomberg framed the reported ambition as a signal that the AI boom has entered its late stage.

As reported, the fund would not target frontier model builders. Its stated goal is to acquire established, largely non-tech companies and improve them with AI, robotics from SoftBank's own unit Roze, and other advanced technologies — a shift from betting mainly on startups toward applying existing AI tools to businesses that already generate revenue.

The reported fundraising push comes days after SoftBank completed the final $10 billion tranche of a $30 billion follow-on investment in OpenAI on October 1, 2026, bringing its cumulative investment in the company to roughly $64.6 billion to $65 billion, or about 13% ownership, according to the article. It also recounts that SoftBank raised $11.1 billion in September 2026 through what was described as the largest high-yield corporate bond sale globally, with the money earmarked for its OpenAI commitment. Critics cited in the article point to SoftBank's concentration risk, the delayed payoff until any OpenAI initial public offering, and a rising debt load.

Gulf backing is presented as familiar territory for Son: the article recalls that his 2017 Vision Fund raised nearly $100 billion, drawing heavily on sovereign wealth funds including Saudi Arabia's PIF and Abu Dhabi's Mubadala, and delivered a mixed record of high-profile gains alongside significant losses. The piece argues that a move from funding frontier AI developers toward retrofitting traditional companies suggests the investment conversation is changing, in line with Bloomberg's late-stage framing.

Per the article, signals to watch include any official confirmation from SoftBank, which Gulf investors commit, and how much of the fund actually materializes, along with progress toward an OpenAI public listing that could convert SoftBank's paper stake into liquid value.

prior_items.title: UBS shares fall as bank launches $6 billion tender offers on legacy Credit Suisse notes
prior_items.summary: On September 2, 2026, UBS Group launched nine separate tender offers targeting legacy Credit Suisse notes, and its shares fell 2.84% to $54.14 after the bank launched the program, slipping a further 0.15% to $54.07 in pre-market trading that day, according to the report. The bank said the program supports proactive funding management and helps optimize interest expense across its capital structure, and the offers could total about $6 billion if holders tender all eligible notes and UBS accepts them. Three offers are structured on an any-and-all basis, covering sterling and dollar securities maturing between 2028 and 2033, including a £750 million note due 2033, a $697.1 million note due 2028, and a $2.25 billion note due 2028, with purchase prices calculated from a reference benchmark yield plus an applicable fixed spread. Six additional maximum-purchase offers cover additional dollar, euro, and sterling debt with outstanding principal ranging from £450 million to $3 billion, subject to a combined $2 billion total purchase cap and acceptance priorities ranked one through six, with the highest priority applying to 9.016% callable notes due 2033. Tenders and withdrawals are due by 5:00 p.m. Eastern time on September 10, settlement is expected on September 14, and holders whose notes are accepted will receive accrued and unpaid interest through the settlement date. The notes being targeted were originally issued by Credit Suisse before its 2023 merger with UBS Group; the merger closed on June 12, 2023, and UBS assumed Credit Suisse's obligations under each affected note series, so the offers address liabilities inherited within UBS's broader funding structure. The bank said it also uses the process to manage total loss-absorbing capacity after absorbing Credit Suisse, and plans to continue issuing senior unsecured debt across major currency markets despite the tender program. The offers carry no minimum principal requirement, do not depend on new financing, and UBS may modify, extend, or terminate individual offers without changing the others.

prior_items.title: ECB and EU regulators move toward common rules for tokenized securities
prior_items.summary: The European Central Bank and EU regulators are working toward a shared rulebook for tokenized securities, aiming to harmonize how tokenized stocks, bonds and funds are treated across the bloc. A common European framework would give real-world asset tokenization a clearer regulatory path, complementing the US momentum seen with the SEC's innovation exemption.
